title: Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index (September 2027), 10:00 a.m. ET
source: EST: the publisher's stated rule, re-read this session off conference-board.org/topics/consumer-confidence fetched direct 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200, 332,031 bytes, verified against its own "Source: August 2026 Consumer Confidence Survey" line) -- "The Conference Board publishes the Consumer Confidence Index (R) at 10 a.m. ET on the last Tuesday of every month." 2027-09-28 is the last Tuesday of September 2027 and a full NYSE session. THE SEPTEMBER RULE IS NOW DOUBLE-SOURCED 3 OF 3, WHICH IT WAS NOT WHEN THIS ID WAS PROPOSED: the proposal cited only the three preceding August editions' next-release lines, because a September edition could not be reached under either slug convention this chain had banked. A third slug form serves them -- CCI-Sept-<year>. Fetched direct 2026-09-06, each verified against its own "Source: September <year> Consumer Confidence Survey" line and each carrying its own "Updated:" stamp: CCI-Sept-2022 (884,195 bytes, Updated 2022-09-27), CCI-Sept-2023 (1,040,855 bytes, Updated 2023-09-26), CCI-Sep-2024 (517,680 bytes, Updated 2024-09-24). Every one is the last Tuesday of its September, and every one matches the release date its own August predecessor announced (CCI-August-2022 "Tuesday, September 27", CCI-August-2023 "Tuesday, September 26", CCI-Aug-2024 "Tuesday, September 24th", all re-fetched this session). The chain forward from each September also holds: those editions name October 25 2022, October 31 2023 and October 29 2024, each the last Tuesday of its October, confirmed against CCI-Oct-2022 / CCI-Oct-2023 / CCI-Oct-2024 fetched the same session. INDEPENDENTLY DATED BY A SECOND PUBLISHER, re-fetched rather than inherited: fhfa.gov/data/hpi (HTTP 200, 89,663 bytes, 2026-09-06) posts a "2027 HPI Release Dates" table whose ninth row reads "Tuesday, September 28 | Monthly Index | July 2027" -- one of twelve 2027 rows, all twelve matching this chain's rule-derived last Tuesdays. That corroborates the calendar arithmetic, never the Conference Board's intentions. Filed estimate because no September-2027 announcement exists: this is the publisher's own rule applied forward against a now-triple-sourced September record. Promote on the August 2027 edition's next-release line naming 2027-09-28. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: CANONICAL FILE written by the consumer-confidence-2027-09-28 initial-research lane (2026-09-06) after reading the one prior proposal, proposals/consumer-confidence-2027-09-28.from-consumer-confidence-2027-08-31.json, which is now inert. Its date claim was re-derived from the primaries rather than inherited and held; one of its three cautions did not. WHAT THE RESEARCH FOUND, none of it in the proposal. (1) THE PROPOSAL'S BLACKOUT CAUTION IS ARITHMETICALLY WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE. It states "the September print sits INSIDE the 2027 FOMC blackout (Sep 4-16 ...)". It does not: 2027-09-28 is twelve days AFTER that window closes and thirteen days after the September 14-15 decision, in clear air that runs 09-17 to 10-15. The 2027 meeting panel was re-read direct this session off federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm (HTTP 200, 166,936 bytes -- NOT the 164,831 five sibling ledgers recorded on this same date, so that page is not the fixed artifact this chain has been treating it as) and reads "September 14-15*", the asterisk being the page's own SEP marker. (2) THE SEPTEMBER PRINT CHANGED SHAPE IN 2025 AND THIS IS THE THIRD YEAR OF THE NEW ONE. The September FOMC decision day has moved earlier every single year -- 2021-09-22, 2022-09-21, 2023-09-20, 2024-09-18, 2025-09-17, 2026-09-16, 2027-09-15 -- while the CB print stays on the last Tuesday. The gap was D+6 in 2021-2024 and is D+13 in 2025-2027. Under the ~16-day field window the editions' own stated cut-offs imply, that flip moves the FOMC decision from OUTSIDE the survey panel to INSIDE it: the 2027 panel runs about 09-05 to 09-21 and contains the decision and its SEP. Only ONE of the five September prints in the 2021-2026 tape window (2025-09-30) has the configuration 2027 will have. (3) AND THE CONFIGURATION IS MEASURABLY NULL, at better power than any control this chain has run on the question. Splitting all 51 clean CB days by whether an FOMC decision fell inside the print's field window gives 16 heard vs 35 deaf, and the two are 0 of 9 across SPY/QQQ/XLY/XRT/AMZN/AAPL/XLF/TLT/VIX (smallest p AAPL 0.0604); CB days within 20 days after a decision vs further out is 0 of 9 at n=24 vs 27. The 08-31 sibling showed the print-day collision carries nothing; this shows the panel CONTENT carries nothing either. (4) THE 08-31 SIBLING'S CELL RULE DOES NOT TRANSFER TO SEPTEMBER. Late August is 6 of 9 narrower than the rest of the year; late September is 1 of 9 and that one leg is TLT WIDER. September is where the summer compression ends -- VIX median 17.20 against August's 16.27 (p=0.0402) and against the Jun+Jul+Aug block's 16.48 (p=0.0072), wider both ways. Read the cell, but read THIS cell. (5) SEPTEMBER'S CUT-OFF LAGS ARE THE TIGHTEST IN THE CHAIN: 7 / 8 / 7 days (2022-09-20, 2023-09-18, 2024-09-17), a 1-day spread against August's 3 and July's 3. The proposal's caution against projecting off its single observation was right in principle and the range it feared is not there. (6) JACKSON HOLE IS ANSWERED AT n=6 FROM A REACHABLE PRIMARY. kansascityfed.org timed out again this session, but federalreserve.gov's own speech indexes date the chair's keynote 2021-08-27, 2022-08-26, 2023-08-25, 2024-08-23, 2025-08-22 and (from this repo's existing FED-sourced entry) 2026-08-28 -- six for six a Friday inside August 22-28. The August edition has never been able to hear it (4 of 4 keynotes fall after the August cut-off); the September panel always opens after it.
